Pool a prespecified generalized linear analysis of completed datasets

Source: R/analysis.R
catmech_pool_glm.Rd

Fits a generalized linear model ([stats::glm()]) across each completed dataset and pools parameter estimates and standard errors using Rubin's rules with Barnard & Rubin (1999) small-sample degrees of freedom.

Usage

catmech_pool_glm(
  result,
  formula,
  family = stats::binomial(),
  conf_level = 0.95,
  exponentiate = FALSE,
  allow_sensitivity = FALSE,
  cluster = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

result

A `catmech_result` from [catmech_model()], [catmech_pmm()], [catmech_reference()], [catmech_contamination()] or [catmech_impute()].

formula

A prespecified formula for [stats::glm()].

family

A description of the error distribution and link function to be used in the model. Defaults to `stats::binomial()` (for logistic regression). Can be a character string naming a family function or the result of a call to a family function.

conf_level

Confidence level between zero and one (default 0.95).

exponentiate

Logical: if `TRUE`, adds exponentiated estimates and confidence intervals (`estimate_exp`, `lower_exp`, `upper_exp`), commonly interpreted as odds ratios (for logistic regression) or incidence rate ratios (for Poisson regression).

allow_sensitivity

Explicitly allow pooled calculations for sensitivity output.

cluster

Optional name of a column identifying clusters for cluster-robust inference. Each completed analysis then uses the CR1S sandwich, factor (G / (G - 1)) ((n - 1) / (n - p)), built from the unscaled inverse information so that it does not depend on an estimated dispersion, and pooling uses complete-data degrees of freedom of clusters minus one.

...

Additional arguments passed to [stats::glm()] (e.g. `control = list(maxit = 50)`).

Value

A data frame of class `c("catmech_pooled_glm", "data.frame")` containing:

term

Model coefficient names.

estimate

Pooled log-scale parameter estimate.

std.error

Total pooled standard error.

df

Barnard & Rubin adjusted degrees of freedom.

lower, upper

Confidence interval bounds on the link scale.

estimate_exp, lower_exp, upper_exp

Exponentiated parameters and bounds (if `exponentiate = TRUE`).

within_variance

Average within-imputation variance.

between_variance

Between-imputation variance.

m, n

Number of completions and total observations.

family, link

The GLM family and link function used.

interpretation

Inference label.

Details

When the audited value is an analysis predictor, include the analysis outcome among the imputation `predictors`. Imputing a predictor without the outcome biases its coefficient toward zero; a warning says so. In a check recorded in `validation/REVIEW_FIXES_2026-11-07.md`, a logistic log odds ratio of 0.80 came out at 0.61, with 65% coverage of nominal 95% intervals, when the outcome was left out.

Examples

set.seed(123)
n <- 50
df <- data.frame(
  lab = stats::rnorm(n, 10, 2),
  age = stats::rnorm(n, 50, 10),
  y = stats::rbinom(n, 1, 0.4)
)
df$lab_ref <- df$lab
df$lab_ref[11:n] <- NA
# lab is a predictor below, so the outcome y joins the imputation model.
res <- catmech_reference(df, value = "lab", reference = "lab_ref",
                         predictors = c("age", "y"), m = 2, seed = 1)
pooled_glm <- catmech_pool_glm(res, y ~ lab + age, family = stats::binomial(),
                               exponentiate = TRUE)
print(pooled_glm)
#> -- Catmech Pooled GLM: binomial (logit link) --
#> Completions (m): 2 | Observations (n): 50
#> 
#>         term estimate std.error     df    lower   upper estimate_exp lower_exp
#>  (Intercept)  -8.5357    6.8331 1.6939 -43.6640 26.5926       0.0002    0.0000
#>          lab   1.2050    0.8170 1.3122  -4.8278  7.2379       3.3369    0.0080
#>          age  -0.0776    0.0624 4.0811  -0.2494  0.0942       0.9253    0.7792
#>     upper_exp
#>  3.540139e+11
#>  1.391153e+03
#>  1.098800e+00
